title: Hochul cheers chance Democrats will bog Trump down with probes and subpoenas - Whatfinger News Quick Hits
text:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul says she is excited by the prospect of a Democratic Congress smothering President Trump’s agenda with investigations and subpoenas, even while she seeks his help on nuclear power.
Hochul told Politico she welcomes the idea of Democrats retaking the House and possibly the Senate so they can flood the next two years with hearings, subpoenas, and oversight of the Trump administration.
Fox News Digital reported the governor’s comments and the sharp pushback that followed from the White House and New York Republicans.
Hochul framed the strategy as essential to halt what she called corruption and abuse. She also claimed a Democratic majority would put a media spotlight on every move and stop a “flood the zone” approach.
“So, I’m excited about this. When you talk about Trump’s next two years with that Democratic House and Senate, hey, guess what? There’s investigations, there’s hearings, there’s subpoenas, there’s questioning. We’re putting the media spotlight on everything he’s doing and trying to stop his ‘flood the zone’ strategy of doing so much bad stuff in such a short time that you can’t even keep track of it.”
She went further, describing congressional committees, subcommittees, and commissions as tools that would “tie things up.” Hochul insisted the goal was not to freeze the good parts of government, only to stop what she labeled corruption and abuse.
In the same conversation she said Democrats winning both chambers would be “next level, game-changing, extraordinary.”
“We are hoping for the House, but to get the Senate on top of it, next level, game-changing, extraordinary,”
Yet the same interview showed Hochul still wants something from the president she hopes to tie down. She said she has a proposal before Trump right now on nuclear power in New York and wants him to treat the projects as a legacy in his home state.
Hochul pledged New York would build more nuclear capacity than the entire country has added in the last 30 years. She said the plan would cut time and cost in half and deliver low-cost, reliable power.
“I can do nuclear and look, I committed that we’re going to build more nuclear in New York than the entire country has in the last 30 years. I need the president. I have a proposal before him now, how to unlock this and do it in half the time and much less cost. I’ve got a plan. So, those are areas where he can make a legacy in his home state.”
White House spokesperson Lauren Bis rejected the governor’s framing outright. Bis said Democrats have no agenda to improve American lives and only want to continue a decade-long campaign against Trump.
“Democrats have no agenda to improve the lives of Americans, their only agenda is to continue their decade-long witch hunt against President Trump. This administration and commonsense Republicans will continue to secure our borders, restore law and order, putting more money back into the pockets of hard-working Americans, and deliver wins for the American people. The choice has never been clearer: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ obstruction.”
New York Republican State Committee communications director David Laska said Hochul had said the quiet part out loud. He argued that if Democrats win either chamber they will use Congress to thwart the president with phony hearings, and he told the governor to focus on New York’s own problems instead.
“Kathy Hochul said the quiet part out loud, admitting that if Democrats win control of either chamber, they’ll use the powers of Congress to thwart the President’s agenda with phony hearings and investigations. Kathy Hochul should worry less about President Trump and more about the fact that New York continues to lead the nation in outmigration because she keeps us the most taxed, least affordable, least free state in the nation,”
Hochul faces voters again this November against Republican nominee Bruce Blakeman, the Nassau County executive. The governor is already working the Democratic coalition hard in New York City.
She has appeared alongside socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani to drive turnout even while acknowledging his base is uneasy with the partnership. The New York Post reported Hochul calling the arrangement “fine” and describing Mamdani as pragmatic about getting things done.
That same alliance has shown up in other demands on the Trump administration, including joint pressure for counterterrorism money while unspent federal funds already sit unused, as covered in earlier reporting on the funding dispute.
Hochul’s record also includes handing sensitive cases to Attorney General Letitia James, a move that drew national attention when Megyn Kelly weighed in on the Cornell defendants.
Democratic figures keep testing the same playbook of pressure and positioning. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has toured upstate New York while keeping her own 2028 options open ahead of the midterms.
Voters will decide in November whether Hochul’s dual message, cheer investigations of Trump while asking him for nuclear help, lands as oversight or pure obstruction. New Yorkers already living with high taxes and outbound migration will judge whether their governor is focused on them or on Washington fights.
Americans can tell the difference between real accountability and a campaign that celebrates gridlock as the plan.
